pharm: Angiotensin II receptor blocker (ARB); selective AT1 receptor antagonist
quick: Contraindicated; boxed warning for fetal toxicity (discontinue ASAP)
No routine adjustment; caution if volume-depleted; avoid if GFR <30 (peds)
Mild-moderate: start 25 mg once daily; not studied in severe
summary: Losartan is an angiotensin II receptor blocker (ARB) that selectively antagonizes the AT1 receptor, lowering blood pressure without inhibiting bradykinin breakdown (lower cough rate than ACE inhibitors). It is indicated for hypertension, for reducing stroke risk in patients with hypertension and left ventricular hypertrophy, and for diabetic nephropathy in type 2 diabetes. It carries a boxed warning for fetal toxicity and must be discontinued when pregnancy is detected. Key safety concerns include hyperkalemia and hypotension in volume-depleted patients; it is contraindicated with aliskiren in diabetics.
indications: Hypertension in adults and pediatric patients 6 years and older
Reduction of stroke risk in patients with hypertension and left ventricular hypertrophy (benefit not established in Black patients)
Treatment of diabetic nephropathy with elevated serum creatinine and proteinuria (urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio >=300 mg/g) in patients with type 2 diabetes and a history of hypertension

dosage.d: Initial 50 mg once daily; maximum 100 mg once daily
dosage.t: Increase as needed to control BP
dosage.n: Start 25 mg once daily if possible intravascular volume depletion (e.g., on diuretics)

dosage.d: Initial 0.7 mg/kg once daily (up to 50 mg total)
dosage.n: Doses above 1.4 mg/kg or >100 mg/day not studied; not recommended <6 yr or GFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m2

dosage.t: Add hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg and/or increase losartan to 100 mg, then HCTZ 25 mg per BP response
dosage.n: Stroke-risk benefit not seen in Black patients

dosage.d: Initial 50 mg once daily; increase to 100 mg once daily

dosage.n: Not studied in severe hepatic impairment

admin: May be taken with or without food (a meal slows absorption and lowers Cmax but minimally affects AUC)
Administer once daily; may be combined with other antihypertensive agents
Correct volume or salt depletion before initiation, or use a 25 mg starting dose
An oral suspension (2.5 mg/mL) can be compounded for patients unable to swallow tablets; refrigerate and use within 4 weeks
Do not coadminister with aliskiren in patients with diabetes
moa: Losartan and its active carboxylic acid metabolite selectively and competitively block angiotensin II at the AT1 receptor in tissues such as vascular smooth muscle and the adrenal gland, inhibiting the vasoconstrictor and aldosterone-secreting effects of angiotensin II. The active metabolite is 10-40 times more potent than losartan and is a non-competitive AT1 antagonist. Unlike ACE inhibitors, losartan does not inhibit ACE (kininase II) and therefore does not affect bradykinin, accounting for its lower incidence of cough.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to any component of the product
Coadministration with aliskiren in patients with diabetes
relative: Volume- or salt-depleted patients (risk of hypotension - correct first)
Renal artery stenosis, chronic kidney disease, severe congestive heart failure (risk of acute renal failure)
Aliskiren in patients with renal impairment (GFR <60 mL/min)
Concomitant ACE inhibitor or other RAAS inhibitor (dual blockade - generally avoid)
monitor: Renal function in patients dependent on RAAS activity
Serum lithium levels with concomitant lithium

preg: Boxed warning - fetal toxicity. Losartan can cause fetal harm; drugs acting on the renin-angiotensin system in the second and third trimesters reduce fetal renal function and increase fetal/neonatal morbidity and death. Oligohydramnios may cause fetal lung hypoplasia and skeletal deformations, and neonatal anuria, renal failure, skull hypoplasia, hypotension, and death may occur. Discontinue losartan as soon as pregnancy is detected. If no alternative exists, counsel on fetal risk and perform serial ultrasounds; discontinue if oligohydramnios occurs unless lifesaving for the mother.
lact: Not recommended. It is not known whether losartan is excreted in human milk, but significant levels of losartan and its active metabolite are present in rat milk. Because of the potential for adverse effects in the nursing infant, decide whether to discontinue nursing or the drug.
renal: No dose adjustment is necessary for renal impairment unless the patient is also volume depleted. Plasma concentrations and AUC of losartan and the active metabolite increase 50-90% in mild (CrCl 50-74 mL/min) or moderate (CrCl 30-49 mL/min) renal insufficiency. Patients dependent on RAAS activity (renal artery stenosis, CKD, severe CHF, volume depletion) are at risk of acute renal failure - monitor renal function and consider withholding/discontinuing if it declines. Not removed by hemodialysis. Not recommended in pediatric patients with GFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m2.
hepatic: Use a starting dose of 25 mg once daily in mild-to-moderate hepatic impairment, where plasma concentrations of losartan and its active metabolite are about 5-fold and 1.7-fold higher, respectively, than in healthy subjects (total plasma clearance about 50% lower, oral bioavailability roughly doubled). Losartan has not been studied in severe hepatic impairment.

major: Aliskiren (contraindicated in diabetes; avoid if renal impairment/GFR <60 - dual RAAS blockade)
ACE inhibitors or other RAAS inhibitors (dual blockade increases hypotension, syncope, hyperkalemia, acute kidney injury per VA NEPHRON-D; generally avoid)
Potassium-sparing diuretics, potassium supplements, potassium-containing salt substitutes, and other agents raising serum potassium (hyperkalemia)
moderate: Lithium (increased serum lithium levels and toxicity - monitor levels)
NSAIDs including selective COX-2 inhibitors (reduced antihypertensive effect; risk of renal deterioration/acute renal failure in elderly, volume-depleted, or renally impaired)
Diuretics/high-dose diuretics (symptomatic hypotension in volume-depleted patients)
minor: Rifampin decreases losartan and active-metabolite AUC by 30-40%
Fluconazole (CYP2C9 inhibitor) lowers active-metabolite AUC ~40% and raises losartan AUC ~70%
No clinically significant interaction with hydrochlorothiazide, digoxin, warfarin, cimetidine, phenobarbital, ketoconazole, or erythromycin
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; a meal slows absorption and lowers Cmax but has only minor effect on AUC.
interactions.alcohol: Alcohol may potentiate blood-pressure lowering and worsen hypotension/dizziness; advise caution.
interactions.diagnostics: May increase serum potassium; hyperkalemia, hyponatremia, and anemia have been reported. Conversion to active metabolite is mediated mainly by CYP2C9; rare CYP2C9-deficient individuals do not form the active metabolite.

emergency: Angioedema with swelling of the larynx and glottis (airway obstruction) or face, lips, pharynx, or tongue

monitoring: Renal function (BUN, serum creatinine), especially in RAAS-dependent patients and with NSAID/diuretic use
Serum lithium levels with concomitant lithium
Signs and symptoms of angioedema and hypotension
counsel: May be taken with or without food, once daily
Report any swelling of the face, lips, throat, or tongue or difficulty breathing (angioedema)
Light-headedness may occur, especially after the first dose or if dehydrated; rise slowly and report fainting
Do not use potassium-containing salt substitutes or potassium supplements without consulting your physician
Women of childbearing age should know the risks in pregnancy and report a suspected pregnancy as soon as possible
Inadequate fluid intake, sweating, vomiting, or diarrhea can cause an excessive fall in blood pressure
pk: BP effect substantially present within 1 week
Losartan Cmax ~1 h; active metabolite 3-4 h; maximal BP effect 3-6 weeks
~24 h (once-daily dosing); ~25-40% AT1 inhibition persists at 24 h
Store at controlled room temperature; protect from light per labeling
pearls: Losartan is a prodrug-like agent: ~14% is converted by CYP2C9/3A4 to a carboxylic acid metabolite that is 10-40 times more potent and provides most of the AT1 blockade
ARBs do not affect bradykinin, so cough rates are similar to placebo/HCTZ - a good option for ACE-inhibitor-induced cough
Stroke-reduction benefit in LVH (LIFE trial) was not demonstrated in Black patients
Reduces progression of diabetic nephropathy (RENAAL: slows doubling of serum creatinine and progression to end-stage renal disease)
Contraindicated with aliskiren in diabetics; avoid dual RAAS blockade (VA NEPHRON-D showed increased hyperkalemia and acute kidney injury)
Losartan has a mild uricosuric effect and may modestly lower serum uric acid
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume the regular schedule. Do not double the dose to make up for a missed one.
overdose: The most likely manifestations are hypotension and tachycardia; bradycardia may occur from parasympathetic (vagal) stimulation. Treat symptomatic hypotension with supportive care (volume expansion, supine positioning). Neither losartan nor its active metabolite can be removed by hemodialysis.
